title: I can't use Chrome without Gemini's Sidebar anymore
content_html:
Published Aug 1, 2026, 1:00 PM EDT

Irene Okpanachi is a Features writer covering Android devices, laptops, portable projectors, VR headsets, software, and AI recorders for Android Police and Talk Android.

She has five years' experience across the Tech, E-commerce, and Food niches, with over 1,000 posts published. The Tech space is where she geeks out most, particularly Android.

Irene holds certifications in Graphic Design (HerTechTrail), Writing in Plain Language (LinkedIn), and English for IT (Cisco Networking Academy).

Beyond writing, Irene is a gamer, singer/songwriter, food lover, and a Jack of all trades.

It feels good to be back on Google Chrome after a year with Apple Safari.

Google has spent that time bringing its computer browser and Android closer together. My biggest surprise was Gemini's Sidebar.

I left the app before I had the chance to see it evolve. So, returning felt like discovering an entirely different feature.

Using it now feels like the upgrade I expected when I got a new laptop.

The tool has become my companion in many cases. Here's why I rely on it frequently in Google Search.

It's an unconventional copy and paste tool

Who doesn't want a smarter way to move information around?

Traditional copy and paste is efficient enough for a single task. But it has its limits in many of the things I do daily. They include research and unifying ideas across devices and apps.

On Android, I have many ways to get information.

Circle to Search is the most fluid one. It lets me pull answers from my screen without hitting a wall.

Normally, I'd have to copy the on-page context, but it's not possible when the text is part of a UI element like a button, menu, or dialog.

Lately, I've spent more time on Google Chrome to catch up on everything that's changed. I haven't put it down since. Gemini's Sidebar is my second monitor in the experience.

The AI-powered panel expands beside my tabs when I click the Ask Gemini button in the upper-right corner. It reads the tab I'm on by default, and I can add up to 10 more for it to reference.

So, it answers using pages I already have open instead of a fresh search. I enjoy the deep visibility it provides into my research as it happens.

My consumer tech work especially takes me down a comparison trail to find the best device or tool. I like to run these comparisons in tandem with other tasks.

Split-screen mood on PC hits different

It makes the ultimate multitasker out of me

When I need extra space to work in Chrome, I'll right-click a second tab and select the New split view with current tab option to divide the view into two. Then I'll expand the Gemini sidebar to make three.

I never have fewer than five tabs open when doing research, so it's a cleaner way to browse without overwhelming myself.

I'm always scanning past articles on a topic, case studies, official documentation, and more. I used to read each one separately and switch between them a lot.

Now, I group tabs and enter @ to ask what sources agree on and where they contradict each other.

Before I pitch or write for websites, I search for the keyword I'm targeting and open the top four competitor results that are already ranking.

I'll also ask what they have in common in headline length, structure, subheadings, and angle. It tells me what's currently working for that keyword.

Then I'll open their published piece next to my own draft in Google Docs, group both tabs, and ask Gemini to point out what they covered that I didn't.

I shop till I drop my phone

But I'm more strategic about it now

I love to shop. It doesn't matter whether it's clothing, gadgets, or décor. Left alone in a store with an open limit, I've made bad calls before.

I bought my way into debt once because there was no system behind my spending to build savings. I'd just gotten out of undergraduate school.

It doesn't help that the market arranges itself to make your escape hard. Discounts and promotions exist to trigger your impulse buying.

I'm always glad to hand over the cost analysis to a tool that's emotionally unavailable. Bundles are a major red flag for me.

So, I like to group product pages with the individual item pages open in different tabs.

I may go as far as reaching the checkout page and asking it to scan for any auto-renewal, free trials, cancellation conditions, and other terms. I don't want to be blindsided by extra charges.

Next, I'll ask Gemini to add the total costs separately against what the bundle charges, since it isn't always cheaper than buying the pieces on their own.

It helps to pull up the CamelCamelCamel website for Amazon, Google Shopping's price history graph for most other retailers, or a tool like Honey or PriceHistory. They tell me if an item ever sold at the "was" price.

I might resell or rotate out items later, so I'll group the page with eBay, Facebook Marketplace, or local platforms. It helps me know what similar items sell for in used condition.

Master your AI workflow with saved prompts

It takes skill to use Gemini well. Feed it the wrong tabs or a vague question, and it repeats the gap in your own thinking. Thankfully, I don't have to repeat myself multiple times anymore.

Prompting is a large part of getting a useful answer from AI. So, I make sure to save my strategic and complex commands with Gemini Skills and reuse them with a few clicks.

The experience is wholesome, despite the full in-app version not being available in my region. It also requires a qualifying AI subscription elsewhere.

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 8 月 1 日下午 1:00（美国东部时间）

Irene Okpanachi 是一位专题作家，涵盖 Android 设备、笔记本电脑、便携式投影仪、VR 耳机、软件以及适用于 Android Police 和 Talk Android 的 AI 录音机。

她在科技、电子商务和食品领域拥有 5 年经验，发表了 1,000 多篇帖子。 科技领域是她最感兴趣的领域，尤其是 Android。

Irene 拥有平面设计 (HerTechTrail)、平白语言写作 (LinkedIn) 和 IT 英语 (思科网络学院) 认证。

除了写作之外，艾琳还是一名游戏玩家、歌手/词曲作者、美食爱好者和多才多艺。

在使用 Apple Safari 一年后，重新使用 Google Chrome 感觉很好。

谷歌花了很多时间将其计算机浏览器和Android更加紧密地结合在一起。 我最大的惊喜是 Gemini 的侧边栏。

在我有机会看到它的发展之前我就离开了这个应用程序。 因此，返回感觉就像发现了一个完全不同的功能。

现在使用它感觉就像我购买新笔记本电脑时所期望的升级。

在很多情况下，该工具已成为我的伴侣。 这就是我在 Google 搜索中经常依赖它的原因。

这是一个非传统的复制粘贴工具

谁不想要一种更智能的方式来移动信息？

传统的复制和粘贴对于单个任务来说足够高效。 但它在我每天做的许多事情上都有其局限性。 其中包括跨设备和应用程序的研究和统一想法。

在Android上，我有很多方法来获取信息。

循环搜索是最流畅的一种。 它让我可以从屏幕上获取答案，而不会碰壁。

通常，我必须复制页面上下文，但当文本是 UI 元素（如按钮、菜单或对话框）的一部分时，这是不可能的。

最近，我在 Google Chrome 上花费了更多时间来了解所有变化。 从那以后我就没有放下过它。 Gemini 的侧边栏是我体验中的第二个显示器。

当我单击右上角的“询问 Gemini”按钮时，人工智能驱动的面板会在我的选项卡旁边展开。 它会读取我默认打开的选项卡，并且我最多可以添加 10 个选项卡以供其参考。

因此，它使用我已经打开的页面而不是新的搜索来回答。 我喜欢它为我的研究提供的深入可见性。

我的消费者技术工作尤其让我进行比较，以找到最好的设备或工具。 我喜欢将这些比较与其他任务一起进行。

PC 上的分屏心情不同

它让我成为终极多任务处理者

当我需要额外的空间在 Chrome 中工作时，我会右键单击第二个选项卡，然后选择“新建拆分视图与当前选项卡”选项，将视图一分为二。 然后我会将 Gemini 侧边栏扩展为三个。

在进行研究时，我打开的选项卡从来不会少于五个，因此这是一种更干净的浏览方式，不会让自己不知所措。

我总是浏览过去有关某个主题的文章、案例研究、官方文档等。 我过去常常单独阅读每一本，并在它们之间切换很多次。

现在，我对选项卡进行分组并输入 @ 来询问哪些来源同意以及它们相互矛盾的地方。

在我为网站进行推介或撰写之前，我会搜索我要定位的关键字并打开已经排名前四的竞争对手结果。

我还会问他们在标题长度、结构、副标题和角度方面有什么共同点。 它告诉我当前该关键字的作用是什么。

然后我会在 Google 文档中打开我自己的草稿旁边他们发表的文章，将两个选项卡分组，并要求 Gemini 指出他们涵盖了我没有涵盖的内容。

我购物直到我丢掉手机

但我现在对此更具战略意义

我喜欢购物。 无论是服装、小玩意还是装饰，都不重要。 独自留在一家限时开放的商店里，我以前也曾做出过错误的决定。

我曾经负债累累，因为我的支出背后没有系统来建立储蓄。 我刚从本科毕业。

市场自行安排让你难以逃脱，这无济于事。 折扣和促销活动会引发您的冲动购买。

我总是很高兴将成本分析交给一个在情感上无法使用的工具。 捆绑对我来说是一个主要的危险信号。

因此，我喜欢将产品页面分组，并在不同选项卡中打开各个项目页面。

我可能会到达结帐页面并要求其扫描任何自动续订、免费试用、取消条件和其他条款。 我不想因额外费用而措手不及。

接下来，我将要求 Gemini 将总成本与捆绑包收费分开添加，因为它并不总是比单独购买部件便宜。

它有助于调出 Amazon 的 CamelCamelCamel 网站、大多数其他零售商的 Google Shopping 价格历史图表，或者 Honey 或 PriceHistory 等工具。 他们告诉我某件商品是否曾经以“原价”出售。

我稍后可能会转售或轮换商品，因此我会将页面与 eBay、Facebook Marketplace 或本地平台分组。 它可以帮助我了解类似物品在二手状态下的售价。

使用保存的提示掌握您的 AI 工作流程

善用双子座需要技巧。 如果给它提供了错误的标签或模糊的问题，它就会重复你自己思维中的差距。 值得庆幸的是，我不必再重复多次了。

提示是从人工智能获得有用答案的一个重要部分。 因此，我确保使用 Gemini Skills 保存我的战略和复杂命令，并通过几次点击重复使用它们。

尽管我所在的地区无法使用完整的应用程序内版本，但这种体验还是很有益的。 它还需要在其他地方进行合格的人工智能订阅。
